OPResearch · Relative value

Sibling or Universe? Pairs Trading vs. Cross-Sectional Value

Each stock is scored on how cheap it is relative to a reference. The pairs strategy uses its sibling (KO vs PEP, HD vs LOW); the cross-sectional strategy uses the whole universe. Everything else is held constant, so the gap between them measures what the sibling comparison is worth.

Jan 2012 – Oct 2026 · 15 pairs · monthly rebalance · 5bp trading cost · 30bp/yr borrow

Findings

  • On the fundamental signal, pairs L/S Sharpe was -0.51 vs -0.16 for cross-sectional L/S — the cross-sectional version did better.
  • Weakest fundamental pairs by contribution: WMT/TGT (-6.3%), MRK/PFE (-5.4%), UPS/FDX (-4.7%).
  • Fundamental pairs: 98 trades, 32% converged within 6 months; 14 stop-outs cost -1.2% vs -17.8% from all other trades.
  • Long-only fundamental: cheap-sibling portfolio CAGR 14.5%, cross-sectional cheapest-third 13.1%, vs 15.2% for equal weight.
  • On the spread signal, pairs L/S Sharpe was -0.01 vs 0.06 for cross-sectional L/S — the cross-sectional version did better.
  • Weakest spread pairs by contribution: UPS/FDX (-7.5%), WMT/TGT (-5.5%), MRK/PFE (-4.0%).
  • Spread pairs: 274 trades, 55% converged within 6 months; 27 stop-outs cost -26.7% vs +30.7% from all other trades.
  • Long-only spread: cheap-sibling portfolio CAGR 15.4%, cross-sectional cheapest-third 16.3%, vs 15.2% for equal weight.
  • Pairs L/S · fundamental: best sub-period 2012–2015 (Sharpe -0.15), worst 2023–2026 (Sharpe -0.91).
  • Pairs L/S · spread: best sub-period 2020–2022 (Sharpe 0.64), worst 2023–2026 (Sharpe -1.19).

Long/short: pairs vs. cross-section

Solid = pairs, dotted = cross-sectional. Amber = fundamental signal, blue = price-spread signal. These books are roughly market-neutral, so judge them on Sharpe and drawdown, not on whether they beat SPY.

Method

Signals. Fundamental: earnings yield (TTM net income / market cap) from SEC EDGAR, rebuilt point-in-time by filing date. EBIT/EV was the original plan, but oil majors, pharma and banks report no operating-income line and debt tags change names over time, so E/P is the one measure every name supports. Pairs gap = yieldA − yieldB; cross-sectional gap = yieldi − universe median. Each gap is z-scored over a trailing 36 months. Spread: pairs gap = log PA − log PB; cross-sectional gap = log Pi − mean log P; z-scored over 252 trading days and sign-flipped so positive = cheap.

Portfolios. Pairs L/S: each pair has a fixed 1/15 slot; enter at |z| ≥ 1.0, exit at |z| < 0.25 or a sign flip, stop at |z| > 3.0 and stay out until the gap resets. Cross-sectional L/S: long cheapest third, short richest third, 100% of capital per leg. Signals at month-end close, trades at the next close. Cash earns zero, so Sharpe ratios are on total, not excess, returns.

Known biases. The pair list is chosen with hindsight (all 15 pairs survive to today). EDGAR XBRL tags vary by company and year, so some fundamental gaps are noisy. Market cap uses diluted weighted shares from the latest quarter; Visa reports no total share count, so its market cap is scaled from its annual public float, which leaves out its class B and C shares.
